residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must have been ordinarily resident in British Columbia for at least one year immediately before the divorce application (Divorce Act, s.3(1)).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The 1-year separation must be completed before or by the time the application is granted. Divorce Order effective 31 days after made (Divorce Act, s.12).

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: Spouses have lived separate and apart for at least one year immediately preceding the determination of the divorce application.

fault.name: Physical or Mental Cruelty
fault.description: Respondent has treated applicant with physical or mental cruelty rendering cohabitation intolerable.

terminology.custody: Decision-Making Responsibility and Parenting Time (2021 Divorce Act amendments, in force March 1, 2021; BC Family Law Act, SBC 2011 uses 'parental responsibilities' for provincial proceedings, but Divorce Act proceedings use federal terminology)
terminology.maritalProperty: Family Property (Family Law Act, SBC 2011, c. 25)

filingFees.notes: BC Supreme Court filing fee is CAD $200 for a Notice of Family Claim (Form F3), plus a $10 federal Central Registry of Divorce Proceedings fee. If no response is filed, an additional ~$80 filing fee applies for the desk order. Parties who provide a Certificate of Mediation (Form F100) are exempt from the $200 filing fee. Fee waiver available under Supreme Court Family Rule 20-5 for parties who cannot afford fees.

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Federal Child Support Guidelines apply in all provinces

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: SSAG are advisory only — not legislatively mandated but widely applied by BC courts

effectiveDateRule: 31 days after the divorce judgment is made, unless the court varies the effective date or both parties waive the waiting period (Divorce Act, s.12).
certificateNote: A Certificate of Divorce may be obtained from the court registry after the effective date of the Divorce Judgment (Divorce Act, s.12(7)).
notes: BC uses the Family Law Act (SBC 2011) which replaced the Family Relations Act. Family property is divided equally by default. BC Supreme Court proceedings are identified by registry (Vancouver, Victoria, Kelowna, Surrey, etc.).
